children: TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 /
Grid Metals Corp.
("Grid" or the "Company")
announces it has set the date for its annual and special general meeting of shareholders ("
ASGM
" or "
Meeting

") for November 17, 2026 at 11:00am Eastern Time. The ASGM will be held at the offices of Peterson McVicar LLP, Suite 1601, 110 Yonge Street, Toronto, ON M5C 1T4. The management information circular (the "
Management Information Circular
") in connection with the ASGM and other proxy-related materials have been mailed to shareholders of the Company (the "
Shareholders
", and each a "
Shareholder

") and are now available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the Company's website at gridmetalscorp.com/investors/other/annual-meeting-materials/. The record date of the Meeting is October 2, 2026.

At the ASGM, Shareholders will be asked to receive the Company's financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025 and the auditor's report thereon, elect directors for the Company's board (the "
Board
") for the ensuing year, re-appoint the auditor and authorize the Board to fix its remuneration, approve the Company's 10% rolling equity incentive plan (the "
Plan

"), approve a special resolution empowering the Board to determine the number of directors within the range set out in the Company's articles, approve and ratify the Company's advance notice by-law for the nomination of directors (the "
Advance Notice By-Law
"), and confirm, ratify and approve, by ordinary resolution of disinterested Shareholders, the creation of a new control person of the Company (the "
Control Person Resolution
"). Shareholders may also consider such other business as may properly be brought before the ASGM or any adjournment or postponement thereof.
Advance Notice By-Law

The Board has adopted By-Law No. 3 relating to the advance notice of nominations of directors. The Advance Notice By-Law establishes a framework under which registered or beneficial owners of common shares of the Company may submit director nominations, including deadlines for submitting nominations and the information required for a nomination notice to be in proper written form.

The Advance Notice By-Law is intended to facilitate an orderly and efficient meeting process and ensure that Shareholders receive sufficient notice and information regarding proposed director nominees to make informed voting decisions. Subject to the exceptions set out in the Advance Notice By-Law, Shareholders seeking to nominate directors must provide timely written notice to the Company's Corporate Secretary within the following timeframes:
Annual meetings:

Not less than 30 days and not more than 65 days before the meeting. If the meeting is called for a date less than 50 days after the first public announcement of the meeting date, notice may be given no later than the close of business on the tenth day following that announcement.
Special meetings that are not also annual meetings:

Where the meeting is called for the purpose of electing directors, notice must be given no later than the close of business on the fifteenth day following the first public announcement of the meeting date.
Meetings using notice-and-access:

Notwithstanding the foregoing, where notice-and-access is used to deliver proxy-related materials for an annual meeting or a special meeting called for the purpose of electing directors, notice must be given at least 40 days before the meeting. If the meeting is called for a date less than 50 days after the first public announcement of the meeting date, notice may be given no later than the close of business on the tenth day following that announcement for an annual meeting, or the fifteenth day for a special meeting.
If a meeting is adjourned or postponed, the applicable notice periods are calculated by reference to the adjourned or postponed meeting date, or the public announcement thereof, as applicable.

A nomination notice must include the information specified in the Advance Notice By-Law regarding the nominating Shareholder and each proposed nominee, including information concerning the nominee's qualifications, securities holdings and independence. The Advance Notice By-Law also requires updates to that information in specified circumstances. The Board may, in its sole discretion and subject to its fiduciary duties under the
Business Corporations Act
(Ontario), waive any requirement of the Advance Notice By-Law, in whole or in part.

At the ASGM, Shareholders will be asked to ratify and confirm the Advance Notice By-Law by ordinary resolution. If rejected by Shareholders, it will cease to be effective upon termination of the ASGM, without affecting the validity of any act done or right acquired under it.

A copy of the Advance Notice By-Law is included as Schedule "IV" to the Management Information Circular and has been filed under the Company's profile on SEDAR+. Shareholders are encouraged to review the full text for complete details of its requirements.
Control Person Resolution
At the ASGM, the Company will seek disinterested Shareholder approval to ratify Waratah Capital Advisors Ltd. ("
Waratah
") as a "control person" of the Company as defined under the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "
TSXV

"). Waratah participated in a strategic private placement in December 2023, in connection with which the Company granted Waratah certain board nomination rights pursuant to an undertaking dated December 19, 2023. Waratah currently beneficially owns, or exercises control or direction over, 45,289,495 common shares, representing approximately 19.4% of the Company's outstanding common shares, and is entitled to nominate two of the Company's five directors. Shareholder approval will require a majority of the votes cast by disinterested Shareholders, excluding votes attached to the 45,289,495 common shares beneficially owned, directly or indirectly, or over which control or direction is exercised, by Waratah and its associates and affiliates. Further details regarding the Control Person Resolution are provided in the Management Information Circular.
About Grid Metals Corp.

The Company is one of the largest mineral rights holders in the Province of Manitoba with over 250,000 hectares of mineral claims and exploration licenses registered to Grid. The current focus of Grid is its Falcon West Property which is advancing towards commercial production following the release of a maiden cesium resource at the Lucy South deposit. A summary of Grid's mineral properties in Manitoba include:

joint venture agreement with Avenir Minerals Limited ("Avenir"),
which has a 15% interest in the property.

Teck can earn up to a 70% interest in Makwa by incurring a total of C$17.3 million, comprising project expenditures (C$15.7 million) and cash payments or equity participation (C$1.6 million) with Grid. Makwa is located on the south arm of the Bird River Greenstone Belt and contains an open pit indicated mineral resource of 14.2 million tonnes grading 0.48% nickel, 0.11% copper, and 0.37 g/t palladium2.
The

Cu-Ni

) is located on the north arm of the Bird River Greenstone Belt. Grid owns a cumulative 89% interest in the project. The project contains an open pit indicated mineral resource of 32.0 million tonnes grading 0.40% copper, 0.16% nickel, and 0.13 g/t palladium2.
The

Li-Cs

) is adjacent to the Mayville Property, and Grid owns 75% of the project. The project contains an open pit inferred mineral resource of 2.1 million tonnes grading 1.42% Li2O and an underground inferred mineral resource of 4.7 million tonnes grading 1.37% Li2O3.
The
Thompson East
Cu-Ni-PGM

) Property is located east of the city of Thompson in north-central Manitoba and captures a number of high tenor Cu- and PGE-rich magmatic sulphide occurrences that are interpreted to be related to the development of the adjacent Thompson Nickel Belt. The property is subject to an
Option and Joint Venture Agreement with Boliden Mineral Canada Ltd ("Boliden").
Boliden is currently sole-funding early-stage exploration on the property.
The 100%-owned Fox River (Cu-Ni-PGM-Au)

Property located in the Gillam region of northeastern Manitoba and covering 90 km of strike of the highly prospective Fox River Belt - a direct analogue to the Raglan nickel district in northern Quebec.
All of the Company's southeastern Manitoba projects are located on the ancestral lands of the Sagkeeng First Nation with whom the Company maintains an Exploration Agreement.
